---
argmap-version: 0.2
title: "Concept: the four readouts, one of each"
description: "Every gauge in the viewer shows two numbers, and there are exactly four ways a node can come by them. A frontier pin is a number the author wrote on a root, and the solve is entitled to disagree with it. A check-only statement is concluded into and asserts nothing, so its `# check:` is an audit reference rather than an input. A step shows the rate its own slab achieves once the rest of the map has had its say. And a refined step shows no constraint at all: its refinement replaced it in the solve, so the arrow is dashed and the gap is a report rather than a tension. One small map, one node of each kind, so the four readouts can be compared side by side."
---

# ===========================================================================
# A rain-affected cricket match, chosen because it is small and nobody has a
# stake in it. Every number below was picked so that its readout is legible,
# which is the one thing a teaching fixture is allowed to tune for and a real
# map is not. On a real map a badge that will not go away is a finding.
#
# THE FOUR KINDS, and the node that carries each:
#
#  1. FRONTIER PIN            @forecast     0.70 -> 0.680  (2026-09-08, G)
#     Authored, nothing concludes into it, so the pin is a genuine solver
#     input. It still moves, a little: $early argues against it, and a point
#     is a target held at the cap (198 flips, D161 item 2), so the line
#     gives most of the way and the point gives 0.02, past the tolerance.
#
#  2. CHECK-ONLY STATEMENT    @unplayable   check 0.75 -> 0.329
#     Concluded into three ways, so D36 rule 3 forbids a pin. The `# check:`
#     is the author's own holistic judgment, held OUT of the solve so the
#     comparison means something. This is the largest gap on the map and it
#     is the honest kind: the author thinks 0.75, their own mapped reasons
#     deliver 0.30, and the badge is the audit finding that says so.
#
#  3. STEP IN FORCE           $call         0.90 -> 0.896
#     An evidence's own gauge. The authored strength is the rate the author
#     wrote for the rule; the solved value is where the rest of the map
#     leaves the line's coin. Under the counts it barely moves: a keyless
#     line holds 16 flips, and $replay pulling the other way holds the same.
#
#  4. SPECTATOR               $soak         0.60 ~> 0.690
#     A refined step. Its refinement REPLACES it in the solve (D38), so it
#     exerts no force at all and its number is not a constraint. What the
#     readout shows since 2026-09-08 is D51's composition of its own finer
#     steps (S21), against the coarse judgment its author wrote. Dashed
#     arrow, no tension tint: the two numbers are not like for like, so the
#     gap is a report. (The D38 delivered conditional, 0.433 here, is a
#     bench readout now.)
#
# Residual discipline: pins on @forecast, @front, @drains, @reserve and
# @saturated, which are all frontier roots. No pin anywhere else.
# ===========================================================================

@forecast [Heavy rain is forecast through the morning] 0.7: the pin, and the map will disagree with it  # tour: solved-vs-authored
@front [The weather front is running ahead of the forecast] 0.7:
$early [a front that arrives early has cleared by the start] 0.8 ~@forecast | @front: the reason the pin above does not stay where it was put

@drains [The outfield drains within an hour of the rain stopping] 0.75:
@reserve [The tournament schedule keeps a reserve day] 0.7:

@unplayable [Play cannot start at the scheduled time]:  # check: 0.75; tour: solved-vs-authored
$soak [the square holds the water it takes] 0.6 @unplayable | @forecast: the coarse judgment, folded; open it and the finer version is what actually solves  # tour: solved-vs-authored
  @saturated [The square is still wet from yesterday] 0.75:
  $soak-fine [rain onto ground already wet has nowhere to go] 0.7 @unplayable | @forecast AND @saturated:
$dry [good drainage answers a wet morning] 0.5 ~@unplayable | @drains:

@abandoned [The match will be abandoned without a ball bowled]:
$call [a lost start ends a one-day match] 0.9 @abandoned | @unplayable: the rule of the competition, so the rate is high; the line holds it no more firmly than any other here  # tour: solved-vs-authored
$replay [a reserve day moves a match instead of ending it] 0.85 ~@abandoned | @reserve:

# ---- reading the four together -------------------------------------------
# Solved 2026-09-08 (the default reference G, D161; solve_map.py):
#   @forecast   0.70       -> 0.680   (a point at the cap, 198 flips; $early
#                                      bent 0.80 -> 0.639 at its 16 flips)
#   @unplayable check 0.75 -> 0.329
#   @abandoned  no number  -> 0.347
#   $call       0.90       -> 0.896   (inside the 0.01 tolerance: no tint)
#   $soak       0.60       ~> 0.690   (S21: the composition of its own
#                                      steps, the folded readout; the D38
#                                      delivered number 0.433 is a bench
#                                      readout now)
# (Under the retired uniform reference, --reference d36, 2026-08-04:
#   0.600 / 0.298 / 0.338 / 0.866 / 0.457, the last the delivered number.)
#
# The four differ in what the AUTHORED number is doing, not in how it is
# displayed. On @forecast it is an input the solve may move. On @unplayable
# it is a reference the solve never sees. On $call it is a claim about a
# rule, compared against the rate that rule achieves. On $soak it is a
# judgment that was superseded, compared against what superseded it.
#
# One number in the readout is deliberately not on the tour: $early solves at
# 0.643 against an authored 0.8, the largest step gap on the map. It is the
# same kind of readout as $call, just louder, and it is louder because it is
# the line arguing against a pin. Nothing here has to be the biggest to be
# worth reading.
#
# @abandoned carries neither a pin nor a check, which is the fifth and most
# common case: a derived statement whose author had no independent view. It
# gets a solved value and no badge, because there is nothing to compare.
